title: GradientOnlyThirdOrderNonconvex.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of f:E→ℝ; nonconvex objectives are permitted. The initial objective gap satisfies f(x0)−inf f≤Δ.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x returns exactly ∇f(x), for every history and oracle seed. Function values and higher derivatives are unavailable. All parameters, including x0, L₁, L₃, Δ and ε, are public; f is hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GradientOnlyThirdOrderNonconvex.lean: spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Query, spec.Reply and spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: f is C³, ∇f is globally L₁-Lipschitz, and D²(∇f) is globally L₃-Lipschitz in operator norm, expressing Lipschitz third derivatives. L₁,L₃,Δ,ε are strictly positive.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Return one point x∈E satisfying ‖∇f(x)‖≤ε; no second-order stationarity requirement.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The output satisfies the gradient-norm bound almost surely over the joint algorithm and oracle randomness, within the supplied fixed gradient-query budget.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: An established smooth nonconvex stationarity formulation with exact gradient access, a bounded initial objective gap, and higher-order smoothness. The oracle supplies gradients alone.

descriptionHtml:
Gradient-Only Third-Order Nonconvex Optimization

We consider minimizing a possibly nonconvex function f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. The function is three times continuously differentiable, with L1-Lipschitz gradient and L3-Lipschitz third derivative in the induced operator norm, where L1,L3>0. A given point x0∈E satisfies f(x0)−infx∈Ef(x)≤Δ, where Δ>0. The oracle returns ∇f(x) at x. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E satisfying ∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, and ∥⋅∥op denotes the induced operator norm, including for multilinear forms. In particular, ∇3f(x) is a trilinear form on E. The algorithm receives E, x0, L1, L3, Δ, and ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness). The function f belongs to C3(E;R), and its gradient satisfies ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L1∥x−y∥,x,y∈E.

Assumption 2 (Third-derivative regularity). The third derivative satisfies ∥∇3f(x)−∇3f(y)∥op≤L3∥x−y∥,x,y∈E.

Assumption 3 (Initial objective gap). The given starting point satisfies f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ,x∈E.

Queries may be made at any point of E. After the allotted gradient calls, the output must satisfy the first-order stationarity criterion ∥∇f(x¯)∥≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
On a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, f∈C3 has L1-Lipschitz gradient and L3-Lipschitz third derivative in operator norm, with f(x0)−inff≤Δ and L1,L3,Δ,ε>0. The setup provides exact gradients and requires ∥∇f(x^)∥≤ε almost surely; the constructed method is deterministic.

Gradient-only nonconvex stationarity under third-order smoothness: GradientOnlyThirdOrderNonconvex.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) GradientOnlyThirdOrderAcceleration (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O((1+ΔL31/3ε−4/3)⋅[1+1+q⋅log(1+(L1+L31/3ε2/3)Δε2)]) gradient calls, all positive parameters.
(2) (Carmon et al. 2017, Theorem 2) O(ΔL11/2L31/6ε−5/3ℓ) total value and gradient calls. Requires ε4/3≤ΔL31/3 and q≥8. (1): Matches the rate on this range using gradients alone; removes all function-value calls. (1) has a much larger leading constant and needs Δ in addition.
(3) Restarted AGD (Li and Lin 2023, Theorem 1) Derived bound: O(ΔL15/8L31/8ε−7/4) gradient calls, using ρ=2L1L3 and rescaled accuracy. Displayed on ε4/3≤ΔL31/3, q≥8. (1): Rate gain q1/8/ℓ when q≫ℓ8. For L1=L3=Δ=1, O(ε−5/3ℓ) instead of O(ε−7/4) as ε→0. (1) needs Lipschitz third derivatives and L3,Δ; (3) needs only Lipschitz Hessians. Cost ratio ℓ/q1/8 favors (3) when q≪ℓ8 within the displayed range.
(4) (Zhou et al. 2026, Theorem 1.3; precise Theorem 5.2, p=3) O(d2+d4/3ε−4/3) gradient calls. Normalized comparison: L1=L3=Δ=1, 0<ε≤1; (4) assumes a known global lower bound. (1): Dimension-free O(ε−5/3ℓ) in this normalization; smaller total bound when d≫ε−1/4ℓ3/4. (1) is slower for fixed small d as ε→0: O(ε−5/3ℓ) versus O(ε−4/3).

Abbr: d=dim⁡E; q=L1/(L31/3ε2/3); ℓ=log⁡(1+L1Δ/ε2); ρ is a Lipschitz constant for ∇2f; AGD denotes accelerated gradient descent. Complexity counts every primitive oracle call; O hides universal factors.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

namespace LongTails.Setups.GradientOnlyThirdOrderNonconvex

open OracleTemplate MeasureTheory

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  x0 : E
  L₁ : ℝ
  L₃ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.finiteE

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.L₁ ∧ 0 < p.L₃ ∧ 0 < p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    ContDiff ℝ 3 f ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ p.L₁ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (gradient f)) x -
      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (gradient f)) y‖ ≤ p.L₃ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ x, f p.x0 - f x ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    (∀ k x seed, O.answer k (0, x) seed = gradient f x)
  successful p f output P := ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.GradientOnlyThirdOrderNonconvex
